getLawyer.why: If you are arrested or detained in Bahamas, ask for a lawyer and for the Canadian consular office to be notified (Honorary Consul of Canada (Nassau): 1-876-926-1500 / 1-844-880-6519). Sign nothing you do not understand. Dual citizenship is not legally recognized in The Bahamas.

Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs in Bahamas are severe — jail or heavy fines. Contact the Canadian consular office and get a local lawyer; say and sign nothing without counsel.

deadlines.title: Tourist stay up to 8 months; passport valid 6 months
deadlines.rule: Tourist stays of up to 8 MONTHS need no visa. Your Canadian passport must be valid at least 6 MONTHS beyond your departure date. Customs officials may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Bahamas

deadlines.title: Drive on the LEFT; Canadian licence valid 90 days
deadlines.rule: Traffic drives on the LEFT. A valid Canadian licence is accepted for up to 90 DAYS; longer stays require a Bahamian licence. An International Driving Permit is advised.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — Bahamas

book.title: Police, ID, and if you're detained in Bahamas
book.overview: Carry a copy of your passport and keep the original secure; customs officials may ask for a return or onward ticket and proof of sufficient funds. If you are arrested or detained, ask for a lawyer and ask that the Canadian consular office be told. Emergency: 911 or 919. Dual citizenship is not legally recognized in The Bahamas.
your_rights: Ask for a lawyer before answering questions.
Ask the authorities to notify the Canadian consular office.
Ask for an interpreter if you do not understand the language.
Do not sign anything you do not understand.
key_steps: Carry ID (or a copy) as the local rules require.
If detained: ask for a lawyer, an interpreter, and the Canadian consular office.
Save the emergency number (911 or 919) and the consular contact (1-876-926-1500 / 1-844-880-6519).
Report theft to the police to get a report for insurance.
common_mistakes: Not carrying ID or a copy.
Assuming dual citizenship guarantees Canadian consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately on arrest or detention — ask for a lawyer and the Canadian consular office.

book.title: Local laws that catch visitors in Bahamas
book.overview: Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs are severe — convicted offenders can expect jail sentences or heavy fines. Other local rules that surprise visitors: It is illegal to leave The Bahamas with more than 10,000 BSD. Long-line fishing is illegal in Bahamian waters. Drones must be registered with The Bahamas Civil Aviation Authority. Dual citizenship is NOT legally recognized — if authorities consider you Bahamian they may refuse Canadian consular services.
your_rights: The right to a lawyer if you are charged.
The right to have the Canadian consular office notified.
The right to an interpreter in proceedings you do not understand.
key_steps: Do not carry packages or luggage for anyone else.
Learn the local rules below before you go — ignorance is not a defence.
It is illegal to leave The Bahamas with more than 10,000 BSD.
Long-line fishing is illegal in Bahamian waters.
common_mistakes: Assuming rules are the same as in Canada.
Carrying or using drugs because they seem tolerated locally.
book.when_lawyer: As soon as you are questioned about, or charged with, any offence.

book.title: Crime, scams and driving in Bahamas
book.overview: Credit and debit card and ATM fraud occurs frequently, especially in Nassau. Driving: Traffic drives on the LEFT. A valid Canadian licence is accepted for up to 90 DAYS; longer stays require a Bahamian licence. An International Driving Permit is advised.
your_rights: To report a crime to the police and receive a report for insurance.
To consular assistance from Canada if you are a victim of crime.
To drive on your Canadian licence for the period stated, if you meet the conditions.
key_steps: Keep valuables out of sight and bags closed in crowds and on transit.
Use only licensed taxis and check ATMs before using your card.
Carry the required safety equipment and documents when driving.
Report theft promptly and contact your card issuer.
common_mistakes: Leaving valuables in a parked car.
Driving without the required permit, equipment, or insurance.
Ignoring local traffic-zone and alcohol rules.
book.when_lawyer: After a serious collision, any arrest, or a significant theft or fraud.
